Queue submissions raise queue.ShutDown, which submit() catches and treats as completed work, allowing offsets to be committed without processing their results. If processing is slower than Kafka consumption, or one worker gets stuck on the slow item this change targets, queued messages and retained offset-tracking state grow without bound until the consumer runs out of memory. Bound total outstanding work and use Arroyo's backpressure mechanism rather than continuing to accept messages indefinitely."

Accepted queued work is consequently abandoned, work finishing after the last commit is replayed, and a slow worker can remain alive after its fixed five-second join timeout. On partition revocation, that worker can continue processing concurrently with the new partition owner. Graceful close/join must drain accepted work, respect the supplied timeout, and flush final offsets before declaring the strategy finished."

This contradicts the strategy's successful-processing guarantee and the new error-handling test's no-commit assertion; that test normally checks before the one-second commit interval elapses. findings.title: Do not reuse a queue pool after its strategy closes
findings.body: The factory creates one queue pool and reuses it for every create_with_partitions() call, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() permanently shuts down that pool's queues and workers. After a partition reassignment, the replacement strategy therefore receives an already-shut-down pool. Queue submissions raise queue.ShutDown, which submit() catches and treats as completed work, allowing offsets to be committed without processing their results. Give each strategy a fresh pool and offset tracker, or implement an assignment-safe reusable pool lifecycle.

findings.title: Bound outstanding work and apply consumer backpressure
findings.body: queue.Queue() has no size limit, and submit() always accepts another message without rejecting or throttling intake. If processing is slower than Kafka consumption, or one worker gets stuck on the slow item this change targets, queued messages and retained offset-tracking state grow without bound until the consumer runs out of memory. Bound total outstanding work and use Arroyo's backpressure mechanism rather than continuing to accept messages indefinitely.

findings.title: Drain workers and flush offsets before completing shutdown
findings.body: close() stops the commit thread before shutting down workers, and pool.shutdown() sets each worker's shutdown flag before its queue is drained. join() merely calls close() again. Accepted queued work is consequently abandoned, work finishing after the last commit is replayed, and a slow worker can remain alive after its fixed five-second join timeout. On partition revocation, that worker can continue processing concurrently with the new partition owner. Graceful close/join must drain accepted work, respect the supplied timeout, and flush final offsets before declaring the strategy finished.

findings.title: Do not make failed worker items automatically committable
findings.body: complete_offset() runs in finally even when result_processor raises. For example, if offset 100 fails and offset 101 succeeds, the commit loop can acknowledge both and advance Kafka to 102, permanently skipping the failed result. This contradicts the strategy's successful-processing guarantee and the new error-handling test's no-commit assertion; that test normally checks before the one-second commit interval elapses. Failed work needs an explicit retry, skip, or DLQ disposition rather than automatically being marked completed.

findings.title: Compute safe commits from delivered offsets rather than integer adjacency
findings.body: Kafka offsets can legitimately have holes, such as those left by transaction control records or compaction. This loop stops at every absent integer even when all delivered messages have completed. With completed offsets 0, 2, 4, and so on, it commits only one message per one-second commit iteration: mark_committed() removes the previous prefix, then the next iteration reaches only the next gap. This severely delays checkpoints and retains completed offsets unnecessarily. Determine the safe boundary from delivered and outstanding offsets, without requiring numerical contiguity.

findings.title: Reject non-positive queue worker counts
findings.body: The CLI accepts any integer for --max-workers, and a negative value passes through this expression unchanged. FixedQueuePool then creates no queues or workers because range(num_queues) is empty. Every decoded message fails queue lookup, but the strategy catches that failure and marks its offset completed, so a configuration such as --max-workers=-1 silently acknowledges all results without processing them. Validate that the configured queue count is positive and fail startup for invalid values.

findings.title: Close the strategy during test cleanup
findings.body: factory.shutdown() stops queue workers but does not set the created strategy's shutdown_event. The strategy's commit_thread therefore continues running forever after this test, retaining its pool and callbacks. The new uptime tests use the same cleanup pattern and leak additional commit threads. Register strategy.close() or terminate() in guaranteed cleanup so background threads cannot outlive the tests.

findings.title: Synchronize workers before asserting a nonempty queue
findings.body: The worker threads process submitted items immediately, so all ten items can be consumed before get_stats() runs. A zero queue depth is valid at this point, making the total_items > 0 assertion scheduling-dependent and capable of failing in CI. Block processing with an event until the initial statistics assertion is complete, or assert properties that remain valid after workers have drained the queues.
